'''Sano Shrine''' (さのじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Sano-machi, {{ill|Nomi, Ishikawa|Q658912|qid=Q658912}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|Q131281|qid=Q131281}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was prefectural shrine.

=== History ===
From ancient times it was enshrined at Sano with many subsidiary shrines, and from early on had shrine administrators and bettō. It was revered by local people as a famous shrine, and on the enthronement grace occasion of Emperor Montoku on December 8, Kashō 3, it was granted Senior Sixth Rank Upper. Also, Lord Maeda Toshitsune of Kaga Domain especially revered it, visited on April 2, Shōhō 1, prayed for lasting military fortune and peace of the state, and on May 1 of the next year personally served as chief officiant.

In May Meiji 35 it was promoted to prefectural shrine, on December 29 of the same year designated as a shrine receiving official offerings, and in April Meiji 40 the subsidiary Kanda Shrine was merged. In September Taishō 13 the haiden was rebuilt, and in August Shōwa 50 the honden, heiden, and shrine office were rebuilt.

Tsukinami festival is held every month on the 1st and 24th from 10:00 a.m.
At spring and autumn grand festivals there are mikoshi processions, lion dance, and dancing.

=== Precincts ===
* Sacred horse statue: stone-made; date and mason unknown, but said to have existed since ancient times.
* Great chinquapin tree: trunk circumference 21 shaku; splits into four large branches at 5 shaku above ground; said to be over 350 years old.
* Hyakudo mound: formerly used as the starting point for midnight “Ushi-no-koku” prayers.
* Kutani kiln remains: said to be the site where source clay for glaze was discovered and where pottery pioneer Saita Dōkai began the Sano kiln.
* Miketsuyama (sacred garden): in front of the shrine on left and right, for praying for abundant crops.
* Kagura-yama (sacred garden): behind the shrine; looking southeast one sees Mt. Hakusan, and looking north one sees the Kofun site Wadayama nearby.
